PESTLE Analysis Model Framework, Circular Flow Diagram, elements: Central circle labeled 'PESTLE ANALYSIS' with six surrounding circles representing factors: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, and Environmental.
ADDIE Model, Circular Flow Diagram, elements: Five interconnected phases: Analyze, Design, Develop, Implement, Evaluate, each with bullet points highlighting key questions for each phase.

```mermaid flowchart LR %% ADDIE Model - Circular Flow Diagram A["**Analyse**
*Be curious*

• What are the business objectives?
• What are the learning needs?
• What does current capability look like?"] D["**Design**
*Be creative*

• What combination of engaging learning methodologies will we select?
• What will the end-to-end learner experience look like?
• What are the specific learning objectives, and how will they be achieved?"] DV["**Develop**
*Get pilot-ready*

• What draft materials feedback do stakeholders have?"] I["**Implement**
*Dive in!*

• How can we support facilitator up skill to deliver the program?
• How will leaders be engaged?"] E["**Evaluate**
*Be reflective*

• Are we hitting the mark?
• How have learners shifted in skills, knowledge, behaviour?
• What do we need to do differently?"] A --> D --> DV --> I --> E --> A classDef analyse fill:#1f6f8b,stroke:#0b2e3b,color:#fff,stroke-width:2px; classDef design fill:#b9d7e8,stroke:#3a6f8a,color:#0b2230,stroke-width:2px; classDef develop fill:#f04b4b,stroke:#7a1e1e,color:#fff,stroke-width:2px; classDef impl fill:#3c8d54,stroke:#1f4a2c,color:#fff,stroke-width:2px; classDef eval fill:#2f6f4e,stroke:#173a28,color:#fff,stroke-width:2px; class A analyse class D design class DV develop class I impl class E eval ```

Freud's Psychosexual Stages of Development, Grid Diagram, elements: Four panels each representing a stage: Oral, Anal, Phallic, and Genital, with brief descriptions and corresponding illustrations for each stage.

```mermaid

    direction TB

    subgraph GRID[" "]
      direction LR

      subgraph ROW1[" "]
        direction LR

        subgraph ORAL["Oral Stage (0–1 year)"]
          direction TB
          ORAL_TXT["Infant focuses on the mouth.\nFeeding and sucking are primary sources of pleasure.\nFixation may lead to oral habits later."]
          ORAL_ILL["Illustration: baby nursing / sucking"]
        end

        subgraph ANAL["Anal Stage (1–3 years)"]
          direction TB
          ANAL_TXT["Pleasure centers on bowel and bladder control.\nToilet training is a key conflict.\nFixation may influence orderliness or messiness."]
          ANAL_ILL["Illustration: toddler on potty / toilet training"]
        end
      end

      subgraph ROW2[" "]
        direction LR

        subgraph PHALLIC["Phallic Stage (3–6 years)"]
          direction TB
          PHALLIC_TXT["Focus on genitals; identification with same‑sex parent.\nOedipus/Electra dynamics.\nFixation may affect self‑image and relationships."]
          PHALLIC_ILL["Illustration: young child (self‑discovery / family)"]
        end

        subgraph GENITAL["Genital Stage (puberty onward)"]
          direction TB

```mermaid
timeline
    title ADDIE Model Timeline
    1975 : FSU creates ADDIE model for U.S. Army (Branson, Rayner, Cox, Furman, King, Hannum, 1975)
    Early 80s : Steps within phases may change to fit an organization's needs (Watson, 1981)
    Mid 80s : ADDIE changes from a waterfall model to a dynamic model (U.S. Army, 1984)
            : The last phase, "Evaluation & Control," is shortened to "Evaluation" (U.S. Army, 1984)
    1995 : ADDIE is first used as an acronym (Schlegel, 1995)
    1997 : Merriënboer (1997) writes that other ID models can be used in conjunction with ADDIE; thus it is a "plug & play" model
    2000s : ADDIE moves beyond a process model (DeSimone, Werner, Harris, 2002) when used to gain direct intuitive insight into a problem
          : While ADDIE strives to identify on-the-job performance (Branson, Rayner, Cox, Furman, Hannum, 1975), it works best with other performance models
```

SWOT Analysis, Grid Diagram, elements: Four quadrants labeled Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats with corresponding questions for each category, divided into internal and external factors and positive and negative impacts.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  %% SWOT Analysis - Grid Diagram

  T[How to Do a SWOT Analysis]

  subgraph G[SWOT Analysis]
    direction TB

    subgraph Row1[ ]
      direction LR

      subgraph S[Strengths]
        direction TB
        S1["• What do we do well?"]
        S2["• What have our customers or partners told us they like about us?"]
        S3["• In what areas do we outpace our competitors?"]
        S4["• What's unique about our business, products, or services?"]
        S5["• What assets do we own (Intellectual property, proprietary technology, capital)?"]
      end

      subgraph W[Weaknesses]
        direction TB
        W1["• What can we improve?"]
        W2["• What are our customers or partners dissatisfied with?"]
        W3["• Where do we fall behind our competitors?"]
        W4["• Where are we lacking in knowledge or resources?"]
      end
    end

    subgraph Row2[ ]
      direction LR

      subgraph O[Opportunities]
        direction TB
        O1["• What emerging trends can we take advantage of?"]
        O2["• Which of our strengths might be valuable to potential partners?"]
        O3["• What adjacent markets might we tap into?"]
        O4["• Are there geographic locations with less competition?"]
      end

      subgraph Tt[Threats]
        direction TB
        T1["• What is our competition doing?"]

        T3["• What market trends are we unprepared for?"]
        T4["• What economic or political issues could impact our business?"]
      end
    end

    A1["Internal"] --- S
    A1 --- W
    A2["External"] --- O
    A2 --- Tt

    B1["Positive"] --- S
    B1 --- O
    B2["Negative"] --- W
    B2 --- Tt
  end

  T --> G

  %% Styling
